proof: lib/io/secure_socket.dart SecureSocket.secure calls socket._detachRaw before RawSecureSocket.secure.
lib/_internal/vm/bin/socket_patch.dart _Socket._detachRaw sets the old _raw field to null.
_Socket.destroy returns immediately when _raw is null; the old controller subscription cancellation only shuts down receive when _raw is nonnull.
Therefore originalSocket.destroy after the secure future completes does not close the upgraded connection.
SecureSocket.secure detaches before waiting for the TLS handshake.
_RawSecureSocket.connect returns _handshakeComplete.future; the secure path has no handshake timeout timer.
ClientBase abort currently has only the detached old Socket during STARTTLS, or no constructed Socket during implicit TLS.
Generation guards run only when createConnectionSocket/createSecureConnectionSocket eventually resolves.
SecureSocket.startConnect alone does not fix this: it delegates cancellation to the TCP task, whose winning native socket is removed from the connecting set before TLS starts.

recommended_strategy: Retain RawSocket ownership during RawSecureSocket.secure and use a protocol/socket adapter boundary that can close the raw owner until secure handoff completes. Preserve normal certificate/hostname verification.
required_regression: Use a real local TCP peer that either accepts implicit TLS or answers STARTTLS OK, then never answers the ClientHello. Cancel/timeout the provider and assert peer-observed TCP closure before releasing any stalled-handshake gate. Verify no auth command is sent and a subsequent call uses a fresh connection.
